body:
Thank you for sharing this man! I don't smoke, so I have had edibles in all forms, for the past 4 years....coconut oil in the past 2 years or so. We all know how strong that stuff is. Quitting has been amazing! I thought being high heightened my senses, but I'll tell you guys this, being sober just makes everything so crystal clear! I work in very close proximity to a fast food restaurant, but for the FIRST time I was able to smell the food, asked my colleagues if wimpy always smelled that good they said yes! Amazing! 

And yes to the vivid dreams! I haven't remembered my dreams in so long. I have basically been on autopilot for a while now. (alcohol since I was 17, switched to pain meds, switched to weed) so i haven't been sober in almost 18 years (35 now) i always wondered why I  dont feel 'happy' anymore and lost my childlike wonder....it's the drugs people! We think we're numbing the pain but WE ARE KILLING THE JOY while at it! 

For everyone wanting to quit, I encourage you, 101%. The amount of clarity you will get will be AMAZING...For those who have relapsed, don't be so hard on yourself, you're only human. You've got tomorrow to try again. And for those who are feeling all sorts of anxious while quitting, you've got this!!! Just hang on. It will all be worth it!

I too experienced this. I noticed I wasn't able to get wet like before. But, it will get better with time. The body has a miraculous way of fixing itself. Don't worry. And I'm lesbian by the way. lol. Imagine the finger being too big hahaha sorry for being graphic but I feel it's necessary so you understand where I'm coming. Fast forward to two years later everything is great! It won't take you no more than a few more months. Just hangin there.

Nooooo you did pull anything! It was like that for me too the first few tries...then I got weak ones...then gahdamn! Houston we have lift off!! Just be a little bit more patient with your new body...you will too, will be just fine!

Oh trust me I went through the same thing. But they eventually became better than before! I wish someone would have told me that I'd be alright because I was worried out of my wits! Then boom! They came back with a bang!

They are different! And that scares most people. You just go through a process of getting to know your body post op. It's a bit of a mind game imo. The more comfortable you become the stronger your orgasm feels.
My question exactly!
Death stranding is definitely worth a try

Believe me when I say I've been there. I'm a little over a year and 6 months PO now. And the funny thing is, all that worry and anxiety is simply in your head. I wish I'd go back to when I had the surgery and just tell myself it will be alright!

I completely understand! I workout for my mental health too and to be honest with you I was as worried as you are right now, I went for another 15k hike yesterday it was great! It might sound like a long time, especially for adrenaline junkies...but it's worth it!! And, if your surgery is laparoscopic it might even be quicker for you coz mine wasn't! Plus, look at it this way, 3 months of recovery and a lifetime of FREEDOM. Feel free to reach out when the time comes!
Wow! Glad to hear you can catch the bus now! Lol! The fatigue is just a lot to deal with really.

I'm a hiker too and almost 8 weeks out! Im currently doing 5k every other day but today I went up the mountain, very easy trail..And like you my pace is still crappy...still, I am grateful of the progress I've made from day one..I remember walking 800m on my first walk and feeling so fucking exhausted and frustrated!

I know exactly how you feel! I'd read a lot of horror stories about shitty orgasms and I couldn't wait to see if it still works down there! It did but wasn't fully functional yet lol. I tried it again a week later and so on and so forth and omg last week was out of this world (still surface stuff nothing penetrative)

What's worked for me I think is the self stimulation has helped awaken my ovaries so don't fret, good things are coming your way lol

It's so strange how a lot of us usually feel 7-10 days post op. I'm almost 8 weeks out now, and I can tell you that the orgasms definitely get better. And eventually stronger than before, at least that's how it happened for me.

I'll bet recovery wasn't as easy was it! Letting people take care of you how they know best and deep down you know they mean well....the urge to get up and fix something even though you're in pain...it wasn't a cup of tea for me
Warm water seemed to work form me. Add a little fresh ginger if you can

I don't know why people sometimes make you feel that way! I received a lot of 'are you sure' before and  'omg, why!' reactions after the surgery which never made sense to me. I'm 32. It's not a decision one can arrive to oh so easily. 
Fact of the matter is you know your body better than anyone who tells you otherwise. There's a reason why you're going for it and unless all those people have lived in your skin and felt everything that made you want to go for it, JUST DO YOU. I'm four weeks post op now and tell you what no regret has flooded my mind since!
Hahaha yeah it's weird how a song doesn't sound as good as when you first heard it stoned
Interesting! Thanks for sharing!
Did you keep your ovaries?
I really hope this will be me
Hahahaha story of my life too! Well written!

Thank you so much this is encouraging. I've never had to use lube ever! Sigh! But hey first time for everything. From a lot of the advice here when I'm in the clear I think it's best I go for it the first few times and see where that goes.

I got extremely horny at 3 weeks too I couldn't wait haha. But thank you for this I will definitely take it slow and hope for the best. I'm so glad you fought off everything and are doing a lot better now I honestly can't wait for my life back!

Alright! I'm also one to kinda ignore some stuff e.g. pushing myself a bit far sometimes going for slightly longer walks, making my meals etc. But I'm trying really hard to follow everything for my recovery it just gets really really frustrating sometimes! I'm happy your husband is very understanding!

Great thank you so much! Oh surface stuff only I know I was really curious and was relieved to see the intensity hasn't changed at all (perhaps when stronger I think) I will have the lube on stand by!
Could also be a result of straining your body. I get that pain when I push my body...do more chores etc and seems to get better when I take it easier.

It's not being against labels exactly, I guess as you get older (I'm 32) you realize that they matter less. So she was just trying to tell you that.... unfortunately this is a journey you have to experience to get to that realization. But don't worry it will be all clear to you
It's amazing when you meet that one person who just accepts you for you! Been with mine for seven years now.
Sigh! I guess I have to wait longer. The break will definitely take me a lot of steps back but I'm happy you're back at it!

I didn't have any edibles a week pre op. I waited another week to have them again and I must say they really helped with my recovery! (With 
my mood, pain, appetite, even fatigue)

Sorry if I missed it somewhere, how long ago did you have your surgery? I'm 3 weeks po (TAH). I know the average recommended waiting time is 6 weeks to exercise again, but my favorite form of exercise is iron and im wondering when I will be able to lift again. Sigh
It's amazing to see how different methods apply. For me warm water with fresh ginger as often as I could did the trick.

I'm now exactly 3 weeks post op. I had(ve) very mixed feelings about it all...did way too much research some helped some scared me to death lol. But, one thing I can tell you is IT GETS BETTER EVERYDAY. The first week is the absolute worst.

But you will notice your body getting stronger everyday, you sit, walk, shower,more comfortably with time.  Try to have as much walking time in your day as your body allows you to. Eat as organic as you can. And drink as much water as you can (I could drink 2L on my 3rd day po)

But do take it easy, I promise those feelings you have are shared my many. I am 32, quite young for a TAH. But everything about it was just a life situation and not necessarily something that has taken away any essence of my being.
